solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: E-Type going around the fastest possible speed for a car

indicators.note: the E-plus-type letters go around the speed symbol, holding it inside them

parts.note: read as E plus Type, and a type is a sort
c is the physicist's symbol for the speed of light, the fastest speed there is

explanation.surface: A Jaguar E-Type circling a track at top speed.
explanation.walkthrough: The E-Type looks like the Jaguar sports car, but the clue splits it into E and a synonym of 'Type'. 'Going around' puts C inside ESORT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ford Escort is a well-known model of family car, so a car can be an Escort.

clue.text: One that's ruined our best bit of acting?

definitions.text: One that's ruined our best bit of acting?

indicators.note: ruined says the letters of our best plus the acting letter are wrecked into a new order
a bit of the word acting is just its first letter

explanation.surface: An actor complains that someone has spoiled their finest performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruined' scrambles OURBEST plus A, the first letter of 'acting'. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: someone who deliberately wrecks things.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrecker who deliberately damages work or property is the classic picture of sabotage's agent.

clue.text: Grand house on front of Sunday Times has nobody living there now

parts.note: G is the usual abbreviation for grand (a thousand pounds)

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: T stands for time, so two of them make times
to have something is to own it

explanation.surface: A grand country house features on the front page of the Sunday Times, empty now.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Sunday Times' looks like the newspaper, but the two words split: S from the front of 'Sunday', and TT as T twice for 'Times'. The definition is singular-sounding while the answer is plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoned settlements, such as old mining camps, are places where no residents remain.

clue.text: Drug taken by Italian married couple

indicators.note: the drug is taken by, so follows, the Italian

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An Italian husband and wife caught using drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken by' tells us the E comes after IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people in a romantic relationship are informally called an item.

clue.text: US city given doubly wrong- sounding name at lunchtime?

indicators.note: doubly means the sound-alike of the word for wrong appears two times
sounding says what is written down only sounds like the word for wrong said twice

parts.note: a wrong is a sin
one o'clock is lunchtime, and one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An American city whose name sounds twice as sinful when said at lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: CIN CIN sounds like SIN SIN. Lunchtime is 1 pm, giving the Roman numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: Cincinnati is a large city in the state of Ohio.

clue.text: Joke gets one mad

parts.note: a gag is a joke
a means one

explanation.surface: Someone's joke drives a listener crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga is an informal synonym for crazy or senile.

clue.text: With only one small plea to 27 down, beginning to tempt fate

indicators.note: with only one small means one of the two S letters is dropped

parts.note: the plea to Kate is the title of the musical Kiss Me, Kate

indicators.note: the beginning of tempt is its first letter

explanation.surface: A shy plea to Kate, with a first move to tempt fate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With only one' leaves KISME from KISSME. 'Kiss Me, Kate' is Cole Porter's musical based on The Taming of the Shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is destiny, a word from Turkish and Arabic for one's lot.

clue.text: Agreed to try and try again

parts.note: a judge hears, or tries, a case
hear again, in the legal sense of trying a case

explanation.surface: A determined person who keeps trying and trying again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is the legal sense: a court tries, or hears, a case.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry used in Parliament to show approval of a speaker means the same as an exclamation of assent.

clue.text: Food pigs eat? Mostly the contrary

indicators.note: contrary letters are awkward and turned around, so they are rearranged
mostly means the last letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: Asking what food pigs eat, with the opposite being mostly true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' leaves TH from 'the'; 'contrary' then scrambles PIGSEAT with TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Long thin strings of pasta are a staple food from Italy.

clue.text: Incidental remark from a second swimmer

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, a swimmer

explanation.surface: A passing comment heard from a swimmer coming second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' is a fish in crosswords; here the ide.
explanation.definitionFit: A passing comment made in parenthesis, or by an actor to the audience, is called an aside.

clue.text: Marsupial finding some flipping emus soporific

indicators.note: flipping says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone finds some emus boring, with 'flipping' as a mild curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads like a mild oath, but it turns the letters backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The American possum is a pouched mammal, so it is a marsupial.

clue.text: Daily Mail's No.1 royal Romeo

parts.note: a daily is a cleaner, also called a char

indicators.note: the number one letter of a word is its first

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: The Daily Mail's leading royal heart-throb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' is not the newspaper: a daily is British for a cleaning lady, also a char.
explanation.definitionFit: Romeo stands for any ladies' man, and a smooth seducer is a charmer.

clue.text: Play with a theme of strength being destroyed, after losing heart in courtship

indicators.note: being destroyed says the letters of these words are smashed and rearranged
after losing says one letter must be taken out of the pool before rearranging
the heart of a word is its central letter

explanation.surface: A drama on the theme of strength crumbling, set in a courtship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart in courtship' is T, the central letter of COURTSHIP; 'after losing' removes it from WITH A THEME OF STRENGTH, and 'being destroyed' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's comedy about Petruchio courting Katherina is a stage drama.

clue.text: See 13
Writing about current role that's turned up, in which there just might be a catch

definitions.text: in which there just might be a catch

indicators.note: the writing goes about, so around, the rest

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
the Ouse is a river, and a current is a flow of water

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a part is a role

explanation.surface: A script about a part that has come up which might have a hidden snag.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is an English river; 'current' is a crossword favourite for a river. 'Turned up' reverses PART to TRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Devices baited with cheese are set so that a rodent might be caught in them.

clue.text: Oily and obsequious Spanish interjection involving nothing anti-American

parts.note: olé is the Spanish cry of approval

indicators.note: involving means containing, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: agin is a dialect word for against, so anti, and US stands for American
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A greasy, fawning Spaniard who exclaims about nothing in an anti-American way.
explanation.walkthrough: Agin is a dialect form of 'against', so it can stand for 'anti'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both greasy in texture and unpleasantly fawning in manner.

clue.text: See 13
Method by which integrated circuit is affecting the whole body?

parts.note: a system is a method

explanation.surface: Asking how an electronic chip works throughout an organism.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine, a condition or drug acting throughout the organism rather than locally is described this way.

clue.text: Republic of South Sudan's regular visitor

indicators.note: regular means taking letters at a steady interval, here every third one

explanation.surface: Someone who often visits the Republic of South Sudan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular' picks every third letter from SOUTH SUDAN'S: U, S, A. 'Visitor' only dresses the surface, which uses the country's real full name.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States of America is a federal republic.

clue.text: Barman an old king's left for dead

indicators.note: left for dead means one letter stands in place of the other

parts.note: Edgar was an Anglo-Saxon king of England; the 's means has

explanation.surface: A pub worker who abandoned an old king, leaving him for dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barman' is not a bartender but a man of musical bars, a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A composer writes in bars, so is a cryptic bar man; Edward Elgar composed the Enigma Variations.

clue.text: Psychologically manipulate, generally starting with a disrespectful insult

indicators.note: the start of generally is its first letter

parts.note: a slight is a snub or insult

explanation.surface: Mind games that usually begin with a rude put-down.
explanation.definitionFit: From the film Gaslight, the verb means to make someone doubt their own sanity.

clue.text: Mischief-maker's in the Home Counties, meeting English monarch in pursuit of own interests

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Home Counties are the counties around London, in the south-east of England, SE
an elf is a mischievous sprite; with the 's it gives the plural-looking form
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A prankster in the commuter belt around London meets an English king, out for themself.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, in England's south-east, so SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who looks out only for their own advantage is called selfish or egotistical in this way.

clue.text: Tight uniform — leg with no room to unwind

indicators.note: with has the uniform letter held among the others
tight means drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tight uniform leaves the wearer's leg with no room to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' looks like it describes the uniform, but it means drunk and scrambles the letters, giving LONGE before the U goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting room where people relax is a lounge.

clue.text: Drunken tinker appearing as lord? Just first character in today's play ultimately

indicators.note: the lord letter goes in the other two
ultimately means the last letter of each word
only the first character of lord is used

explanation.surface: The drunken tinker who is tricked into thinking he is a lord, the first character seen in today's play.
explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Sly is the drunken tinker of the Induction to The Taming of the Shrew, fooled into believing he is a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Sly, the drunkard who watches the play-within-the-play, is the first character on stage in Shakespeare's comedy.

clue.text: Frightful worry about a growth

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, so around, the single letter
frightful means the letters are in a terrible state, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone frets terribly over a lump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frightful' scrambles WORRY into YRROW, and 'about' puts it around A.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarrow is a flowering plant, and a plant is something that grows.

clue.text: Heading away from square, cycling round to the Central Line

indicators.note: the cycled letters go round the next word
cycling moves the end letter round to the front
the heading, or first letter, of square goes away

explanation.surface: A commuter leaves the square and cycles round to the Central Line on the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading away from' leaves QUARE; 'cycling' brings the E to the front, EQUAR, and 'round' wraps it around TO. The Central Line is a London Underground line.
explanation.definitionFit: The imaginary circle round the middle of the Earth is literally a central line.

clue.text: Goodbye to All That's leading parts are about to be cast

indicators.note: the leading parts of words are their first letters
to be cast off means taken away from the word

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: The lead roles in a production of Robert Graves's memoir Goodbye to All That are about to be cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To be cast' removes RE (about) from ARE, leaving A. Goodbye to All That is Robert Graves's memoir.
explanation.definitionFit: Ta-ta is an informal British farewell, a casual way to say bye.

clue.text: More perverted relations with heartless killer

parts.note: kin are one's relations

indicators.note: heartless means the middle of the word is taken out

explanation.surface: Family members who are even more depraved, and a cruel murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' takes the middle LL from KILLER, leaving KIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinky describes unconventional sexual tastes, so the comparative means more depraved.

clue.text: Female swimmer's first off

indicators.note: first off means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: the skate is a flat fish, a swimmer; the 's means is

explanation.surface: A woman swimmer is off the blocks first.
explanation.walkthrough: A skate is a flat sea fish; 'swimmer' often means fish in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Kate is a woman's name, so a female, and Katherina is the shrew of the theme play.

clue.text: Bar serving gin to drunk

indicators.note: drunk letters reel about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bar that serves gin to a drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub, but here it is a bar of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast block of metal, typically gold, is shaped like a bar.

clue.text: A leading role in conversion of useless picture house

indicators.note: conversion means the letters are changed into a new arrangement
useless means the letters of use are removed

explanation.surface: A star part in the conversion of a disused cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: A picture house is an old British term for a cinema. 'Useless' strips USE from HOUSE, and 'conversion of' rearranges PICTUREHO.
explanation.definitionFit: Petruchio is the male lead in The Taming of the Shrew, wooing Katherina.
